summary: Classic house (Chicago and 90s, not deep house): 120-126 BPM TR-909 four-on-the-floor, claps on 2 and 4, off-beat open hats, a bouncy off-beat synth bass, stabbed piano or organ chords in a 2-4 chord loop; knowledge/style/house.json is its template
body: Tempo 120-126 BPM, usually 122-124; toward 128-130 it becomes tech house and techno.

Drums: a TR-909 (707 and 808 sounds too): kick on every beat, clap or snare on 2 and 4, open hat on every off-beat, closed hats and a shaker in 16ths, a crash on the phrase; 16th swing on the hats (every second 16th late) is what makes it jack. Patterns change every 4, 8 or 16 bars.

Bass: a punchy, short synth bass (CZ, FM or analog) in the mid-low register, syncopated on the off-beats around the root, often minor pentatonic; the kick owns the sub and the bass ducks under it (sidechain).

Harmony: one- to four-chord loops, minor 7ths and 9ths (i7-VII-iv7-VI, or the pop I-V-vi-IV); classically a sampled jazz or soul chord, an M1 piano or an organ, played as short off-beat stabs, not held pads.
Lead: a vocal hook, an organ or piano riff, or a bright synth hook; often the melody is just the top note of the chords.
Texture/master: clean and punchy, most parts high-passed to leave the kick and bass alone, the bass sidechained to the kick, light bus compression and a limiter; no lofi roll-off.

Sources (2026-11-26): EDMProd 'How To Make House Music'; MusicRadar 'Beat Building: how to make a classic house beat'; Native Instruments 'Progressive house' (909 claps on 2 and 4, piano chords, sidechained bass).

Apply: pattern/four-on-the-floor on the drums, then pattern/prog-house-characteristic-2 on the keys four bars later. For a whole style change the Team Lead's restyle uses knowledge/style/house.json instead.

drums.about: the drum track (a kit); leave out if there isn't one

keys.about: a chordal part (keys, pad); leave out if there isn't one

key.about: the project's key; leave out to estimate it from the notes
